title: Sonnet Self-Reflection Core
desc: Sonnet reflex core: verify-before-trust, no-stop-menu, delegate-first, live-fire-proof, guard-source-first, anti-noise-injection, mechanical-enforcement-over-documentation. T2 howto / T3 ref hold patterns and dated incidents.
steps: DECISION: a READ-ONLY sector must be briefed to WRITE ONE EVIDENCE FILE under .tmp/ at a path ROOT names, because the debrief gate reads a STRUCTURAL trace -- a commit, a passing test, a scored skill edit -- and a perfect read-only report leaves none of the three, so the gate charges the round as an ambiguous failure and BLOCKS THE NEXT DISPATCH. WHEN: dispatching any audit, survey, parity check or coverage measurement, which is exactly the class that produces no artifact by nature. HOW: name the file in the brief (for example .tmp/parity_audit.md), make writing it an exit criterion, and re-run one of the sector's own commands from ROOT's seat the moment it returns -- run wkappbot skill read agent-debrief-gate for what the gate inspects and wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-howto for the run-it-never-read-it rule. WHY: measured 2026-09-07 in WkAutoQuant. A read-only triage sector returned a genuinely correct report -- it counted 15 wired-protos at the top level of .tmp where the descent gate had said 29, and ROOT's own re-run confirmed 15 top-level against 31 recursive, so BOTH numbers were true under different patterns and the sector had honestly named its pattern. The work was good and the gate still blocked the next dispatch, because good work with no artifact is indistinguishable from a narrative success claim. THE RULE THAT SURVIVES: a count is only a finding when the PATTERN that produced it is quoted beside it, and a measurement sector is only complete when its measurement exists as a file somebody else can open. //why:agy survey confirmed no env section in  -- agy DEFECT 1 needs different injection approach //why:items 3+4 survey returned: CodexPreToolPolicy.ps1 line 76 blocks FromBase64String; Agent.ps1 lines 275-292 has no deliverable-absent check //why:verified fix on origin/main by delegating read+run to haiku; remote blob confirmed no sys.path.insert, 40/40-sonnet //why:Explore subagent type is read-only; use general-purpose for proto-write tasks-sonnet //why:Sectors B and C wrote evidence files; ghostwrite confirmed 143/144 lines, patrol fills verified-haiku

DECISION: grep sibling copies before declaring a fix closed -- and read the surrounding design-rationale comments too, not just the code shape, before accepting a delegate's plausible fix (2026-08-17 near-miss on the Stop-hook size gate). -- duplicated logic drifts independently across a repo. WHEN: about to call any bug fixed. HOW: grep the whole tree for the same pattern and check whether each hit runs at the same processing stage as the one you patched -- wkappbot skill read sonnet-reflection-ref-t3 for the five duplicate-drift bugs found on 2026-07-15 alone. WHY: a fix correct at one stage can be a no-op at a sibling copy. //why:wish-gate blocks deletion: selftest has no caller, must wire before deleting paragraph-sonnet //why:patrol-after haiku ran gh run list+view directly; APBK0918x150 confirmed market-closed normal, FLAG=NONE, no Traceback-haiku //why:load-once guard for dot-source at PreToolUse line: verifying single-line form stays net-zero for fat-source-growth gate-sonnet

DECISION: wiring canonical is ROOT's own charge, never a cheap-tier delegation. COMMIT EACH PROMOTION SEPARATELY (2026-08-09): when promoting 2+ independently-verified protos in one turn, git add -f + git mv -f + commit EACH ONE before starting the next, rather than batching them into one pending commit -- a single leftover defect (e.g. one non-ASCII literal) in file B's staged content blocks the pre-commit hook for BOTH files at once, forcing a revert of file A's already-good work too, and can make an innocent agent's correct dispatch look like a failure to the debrief gate. WHEN: a cheap agent has finished a proto plus self-test for a canonical change. HOW: ROOT alone reviews the diff and runs git add/commit on the canonical file, even under time pressure -- wkappbot skill read proto-to-live-wiring for the three-artifact contract. WHY: a cheap agent must never hold both design and live-wiring responsibility, or ROOT loses the personal-review checkpoint. //why:Update-WkKeywordIndex before match loop caused No matches found; moved to after loop with try/catch, verified proto finds 30+ sessions //why:live-fire proved the tell ownership guard both directions before reporting it done-sonnet //why:sector copy-to-canonical needed because E3 blocks git mv on Agent.* harness files at ROOT-sonnet //why:Update-WkKeywordIndex before match loop caused No matches found; moved to after loop with try/catch, verified proto finds 30+ sessions-sonnet

CONFIRMED 2026-09-09: a commit-only dispatch was correctly scoped (mechanical, no judgment), but the parent should have checked the letter's byte-growth against HEAD BEFORE dispatching -- the first round burned a full dispatch on a fat-md-growth refusal that a single wc -c comparison would have caught in advance. FOUR TOKEN-BURNING TRAPS MEASURED 2026-09-13 ACROSS A TEN-HOUR DESCENT, left here because the next session may be token-poor and each of these costs rounds rather than minutes. ONE, NEVER PIPE git commit THROUGH tail OR head: the pipeline reports the FILTER's exit code, so a BLOCKED commit reads as success and the work looks landed when it is not -- done twice in one session before it was noticed. TWO, NEVER STAGE HANDOFF.md BESIDE SOURCE: the letter gates key on a STAGED letter, so a leftover git add attaches the whole letter ladder to unrelated source commits and the refusal names the letter while the diff does not -- six times in one session. git restore --staged HANDOFF.md and the same commit passes unchanged. THREE, TRIM THE LETTER IN THIS ORDER, because at three minutes a commit the order IS the saving: move the passage into a SKILL and leave a pointer, which is the biggest cut and the gate's own remedy; delete a paragraph whose fact already sits in a MANIFEST row, since the row carries the sha permanently; drop the instruction of a wish you EXECUTED this session and keep only the rules it bought; merge manifest rows without losing one sha; and REWORD SENTENCES LAST, worth only a hundred to three hundred bytes and the trap if done first. FOUR, READ THE SCORE BEFORE --add-step: under 70 the edit guard refuses it and under the floor it seals every lock naming that skill, so merge with --find/--replace instead -- this core sits at 23 steps against its own 19-to-20 ceiling and one added step refuses EVERY delegation the fleet makes. AND EXPECT A LADDER: the letter gates arrive as wish-ratchet, then anchor, then size, each refusal naming only its own rung, so clearing one reveals the next rather than finishing the work. DECISION: search the skill tree the moment an unfamiliar term appears, bare keyword or embedded mid-sentence. ROOT-SIDE COROLLARY 2026-09-08: before dispatching a tiny busy-fleet-reset verification sector, check whether an already in-flight sector (blocked and awaiting my input) could satisfy the same freshness window instead of firing a fresh one that then gets classified as an ambiguous failure for reporting the very block it was sent to clear. WHEN: an unfamiliar term shows up before improvising a fix or guessing at a mechanism. HOW: check --help and wkappbot skill search before concluding a capability gap exists -- wkappbot skill read sonnet-reflection-ref-t3 for the dated incidents this rule came from. WHY: absence-of-evidence-in-memory is not evidence-of-absence-in-the-tool. //why:busy-fleet/clean-baseline deadlock: committed verification comment via single-line message, proto+git mv for omega-guarded file-sonnet //why:write-target guard blocks PowerShell @heredoc for git commit; use Write tool to write .tmp/commit-msg.txt then single Bash git commit -F; stash dirty global-CLAUDE.md before Agent.cmd delegation (clean-baseline guard)-sonnet //why:write-target guard blocks PowerShell @heredoc for git commit; use Write tool to write .tmp/commit-msg.txt then single Bash git commit -F; stash dirty global-CLAUDE.md before Agent.cmd delegation (clean-baseline guard)-sonnet

A BRIEF IS REFUSED ONCE PER MISSING PART AND EACH REFUSAL NAMES A DIFFERENT ONE -- assemble the whole shape before sending rather than discovering it four times. WHEN: firing any sector, and above all a fan-out, since every sibling in the message pays the same toll. MEASURED 2026-09-19 dispatching three disjoint sectors: refusal one, the brief named a -ref tier as required reading, and brief-reftier-gate wants the core or the -howto because a dated incident archive teaches a cheap tier the SHAPE of a past failure instead of the rule that prevents it. Refusal two, no model field -- an omitted model INHERITS THE CALLER'S, so from an Opus root it silently spawns Opus at the top rate, and a guard matching the word opus has nothing to match when the field is simply absent. Refusal three, the five labels Goal/Files/Approach/Constraints/Exit were missing. Refusal four, the three artifacts plus a FENCED code sample and a CALL-SITE sample were missing, and indented code is NOT detected -- it must be three backticks. THE COMPLETE SHAPE, assembled once (MEASURED 2026-09-20: two of three near-identical briefs were refused as missing Files or Approach while the third passed, all three written as FILES you own and APPROACH followed by a period; the resend that used the plain line-leading colon labels Goal: Files: Approach: Constraints: Exit: passed all three, so write the five labels that way and do not rely on a paren or a period after the label): an explicit CHEAP model tier (a dispatch to the mid tier is refused without condition since 2026-09-20, commit 6e93a36eb, so there is no reason code to state), the five labels, three-plus skill reads that are cores or -howto tiers including the dispatched model's own reflection, one verbatim quoted sentence from a named skill, module proto and wired proto and self-test as named ABSOLUTE paths under .tmp, a fenced module sample, a fenced call-site sample so the signature matches what ROOT will install, and an Exit that asks the sector to COUNT the artifacts back. AND EVERY GUARD WAS RIGHT: a delegate handed a -ref tier, an inherited model and no call-site sample returns a module whose signature the host cannot call. THE COST OF LEARNING THEM ONE AT A TIME: every retry re-sends the entire brief, so four refusals cost four times the tokens and buy nothing. //why:discovered 5 missing brief parts one at a time instead of assembling the full shape before first dispatch //why:assembled all 3 artifacts + call-site + fenced sample before dispatching both proto sectors-sonnet //why:brief-three-artifacts + brief-reftier-gate + brief-wiring-gate fired in sequence on item5 sector dispatch -- assemble the full shape including fenced code block before sending-sonnet //why:discovered 5 missing brief parts one at a time instead of assembling the full shape before first dispatch-sonnet

DECISION: delegate the thing you do not want to do, first, not last (2026-09-09: dispatched a cross-repo guard-fix proto build to Haiku for the wkappbot-kih letter-edit bugs, kept the wiring/review for ROOT). FORK NOTE 2026-09-08: a forked worker has NO subagent-spawn rights and the knowledge-op stall-reset was removed by owner directive the same day, so when a fork hits stall-guard mid-task, keep working through read-only and skill-edit calls, which stay pace-exempt, and land file edits via the sanctioned wkappbot file edit or file write route rather than looping retries on the exact blocked call. STATED AS THE SANCTIONED ROUTE AND NOT AS A HOLE: file edit is the reviewed path a study lock expects, so reach for it because it is correct, never because it is 'not gated the same way' -- a remedy remembered as a gap is one a successor widens.. AND WHEN THE CHEAPEST TIER PHYSICALLY CANNOT RUN, THAT IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A PREFERENCE -- measured 2026-09-06 in WkAutoQuant, where the SAME read-only four-command brief died FIVE times on haiku with Prompt is too long, HTTP 400, before its first command, including once cut to a quarter of its length, because the project CLAUDE.md alone fills that window; the identical brief on sonnet completed and returned every number. The closed-list token for that escalation is HAIKU-FAILED-TWICE and it must be EARNED by two already-sharpened attempts, never assumed -- but once earned, continuing to re-send a haiku is not thrift, it is burning a round per attempt on a wall that a shorter brief cannot move. THE REPAIR IS UPSTREAM: shrink what is injected into every subagent prompt, and re-test the cheap tier afterwards rather than leaving the escalation permanent. WHEN: a task feels like the one you would rather skip, defer, or quietly avoid. HOW: delegate it or do it immediately (SONNET ROOT 2026-09-28: when stall-guard says delegate, the delegation itself must pass the brief-guard -- executed wkappbot skill read lines at the top of a .md file, then Agent.cmd --model haiku --file; a sonnet rookie spent an hour re-sending inline briefs refused 1/3 while its deliverable sat unchanged, and a headless root that promises ScheduleWakeup instead of doing the check simply ends its run) -- wkappbot skill read sonnet-reflection-ref-t3 for the CRITICAL-FIRST-file incident this rule came from. WHY: writing another status update around an avoided task costs more than just doing it. MECHANISM (banked 2026-08-09, user asked directly why solo hands-on work degrades quality): doing exploratory/mechanical work personally pulls raw tool-output noise into ROOT's own context; a larger session file compacts sooner and more often, compaction loses earlier nuance, and judgment made on top of lost context degrades -- repeated questions, forgotten prior answers, visibly worse behavior. Not a capability change -- a context-budget consequence. Delegating keeps that noise in a subagent's disposable context and leaves this one lean. FOLLOWUP 2026-08-17 (three self-caught mistakes, one session): cited tier-gate as the reason wkharness-guards skill bloat could not be fixed, when skill editing is a knowledge-op never gated by tier-gate/busy-fleet/pace -- the user named this as laziness dressed as compliance. Separately began a session-content-truncation investigation by manually ls-ing raw JSONL files instead of wkhippo recall, wasting tokens the dedicated tool exists to avoid, then tried to abandon that same investigation as too hard before being told directly to keep pulling the thread via git log/git blame plus wkhippo. WHEN extended: before citing any gate as a blocker, verify the operation is actually gated; before manually searching session history, use wkhippo recall; before dropping a hard investigation, exhaust git log/git blame first. WHY extended: all three were the easy wrong path chosen over the slightly harder right one, caught by the user in a single session, not by self-discipline. //why:Run the sector's real call from my own seat: a passing structural selftest hid a null return.-sonnet //why:A sector's static diagnosis must be confirmed by reading the named line before a fix is dispatched.-sonnet //why:A sector's static diagnosis must be confirmed by reading the named line before a fix is dispatched.-sonnet //why:items 1+2 survey found: no one-command rule in codex prepend; file-edit error at FileToolCommands.Edit.cs:355 via EscapeDecodeSpec

DECISION: a plausible cause that explains the symptom is not the cause -- confirmed live -- confirmed live. WHEN: you have a confirmed symptom and a theory that accounts for it, and a fix follows obviously from the theory. HOW: read the actual code and reproduce the failure against the real pattern before touching anything -- wkappbot skill read sonnet-reflection-ref-t3 for the 2026-07-16 incident where a theory would have removed a real security control. WHY: fix what the reproduction proves, not what the theory predicted -- the symptom can match multiple explanations equally well. DATA IS REMOTE-FIRST, SOURCE IS LOCAL-FIRST, measured 2026-09-25 as a Sonnet ROOT under the spokesman: it escalated an expired US token and proposed live validation inside token_is_usable, when its own checkout was a detached branch 9 days stale and git show origin/main of the same token file was valid, committed that evening. Before diagnosing ANY data-driven failure (tokens, caches, state files, prices) read the origin/main copy first; a stale checkout produces a confident, reproducible, wrong diagnosis. The fix that landed (c99ba5417c) was to make the tool adopt the newer origin blob, not to weaken the expiry check. AND GIVE YOURSELF ONE MEASURABLE DELIVERABLE: a sibling Sonnet ROOT given the open order process HANDOFF.md spent its whole run on the letter commit gates and ended with its only commit pending, while the one given a concrete report with named tools produced findings and a landed fix. //why:HANDOFF.md reconstruction must use origin/main as base, not local HEAD, so stale-guard passes on push //why:A sector's DIFF claim that the indexer cannot answer pending agents was its own wrong call, my direct run returned ok with counts.-sonnet //why:A sector's DIFF claim that the indexer cannot answer pending agents was its own wrong call, my direct run returned ok with counts.-sonnet //why:HANDOFF.md reconstruction must use origin/main as base, not local HEAD, so stale-guard passes on push-sonnet //why:exec hotswap fix c410edfae6 confirmed on origin/main via git branch -r --contains before reporting //why:the haiku probe-file location was a real anti-pattern, verified by reading the actual write, not assumed //why:Sector E confirmed: SID prefix vs full UUID mismatch, not wrong brain dir path; exact-match at line 78 is root cause //why:git branch -r --contains returns empty after wkpush rebase; use git log origin/main to verify pushed commits -- local hash differs from rebased remote hash //why:verified aggr-pyramid A/B replay: 0 [aggr-pyramid] tags on both dates because condition never triggered, not because the seam was wrong

DECISION: live-fire is the only proof a guard works, and the sharpest form of it is the NULL-ACTION CHECK -- ask what your test would report if the code under it did NOTHING AT ALL, and if it would still go green the test is measuring the wrong thing. Measured three ways on 2026-08-28 in WkAutoQuant: a duplicate-buy case seeded its tracked entry ALREADY at the test price, so the skip fired on iteration one, the broker was called zero times, and a fully stubbed-out function would have passed it; a dependency-hiding case deleted its target from sys.modules IN-PROCESS, which does not sever an already-bound reference, so it reported green while the dependency was plainly still working; and a NaN guard whose finite-check was inverted returned the safe answer for the wrong reason and its own suite called that case PASS. All three were found in seconds by probing the artifact from OUTSIDE its own suite. Pair every gate with its inversion control -- two inputs that must produce OPPOSITE verdicts -- because a suite with no such pair cannot tell a working mechanism from an absent one. WHEN: a guard has just been wired and its self-test is green. HOW: attempt the actual forbidden action and confirm it BLOCKS, then the legitimate action and confirm it PASSES, both directions, on real data -- wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static for the method. WHY: a green self-test proves the function works on its own fixtures, nothing more -- this repo has caught fully-inert guards this way multiple times. SAME RULE 2026-09-20: a haiku self-test ignored its own --module argument, so a sabotaged module passed through it still scored 8 of 8 while the sector report claimed a red null control; accept a null control only after passing a sabotaged copy through the tested parameter yourself and seeing the named cases go red. //why:Sector C confirmed trace fails before agy correlation fix is wired; expected outcome validates the repair scope //why:verified item1 fix by reading file content on origin, not hash, after wkpush -m promotion //why:Module selftest 4/4 with BUY cancel fired and SELL inversion refused -- live-fire proof both ways-sonnet //why:Ran the landed beat myself and found two defects the sector self-test never exercised.-sonnet //why:verified item1 fix by reading file content on origin, not hash, after wkpush -m promotion-opus

DECISION: VERIFY A LIVE-TRADING SEAM ON FOUR NUMBERS, NOT ON A GREEN FEELING -- the line count, the lint findings, the compile exit code, and the EXECUTED case count. Measured 2026-09-07 while a market was open: a one-line price fix at host 822 had to prove it did not grow a file already at its 2039-line cap, did not introduce an undefined name that would raise inside a one-second loop, still compiled, and left the host suite at its full 87 executed cases. That last number is the one that hides a crash: a suite dying midway prints a SUMMARY tally that reads exactly like a smaller healthy suite, so count the PASS and FAIL lines yourself rather than believing the tally. A DISPATCH THAT NEVER RAN IS NOT YOUR FAILURE, AND ROOT MUST NOT CHARGE IT TO YOU. Measured 2026-09-07 late in a long session: four consecutive briefs were refused by the debrief gate BEFORE the agent started, because an earlier round's reflection debt was unpaid -- so the gate reported them as failed missions that had produced nothing, which is true and tells you nothing about the brief. ROOT's move is to read the gate board BEFORE fanning out rather than discovering the debt one refusal at a time; a sector that never received its prompt cannot be sharpened by rewriting the prompt. WRITE AN EVIDENCE FILE WHEN YOUR MISSION IS READ-ONLY. Measured 2026-09-07: three measurement sectors answered correctly and all three were graded FAILED, because the debrief gate looks for a commit, a passing test or a scored skill edit, and a census produces none of those. Your correct answer then costs the dispatching session a reflection round before it can ask you anything else. So when the task is to COUNT, MEASURE or SURVEY, write your table and every raw command output to a file as you go and name that path in your report -- it is the structural trace the gate needs, and it is also what ROOT should re-read instead of trusting your summary. AND STAND BY A REFUSAL: declining to pass a cumulative figure off as a dated one is the right answer even when it reads as UNAVAILABLE, and it should be reported as a finding rather than softened. NO STOP-MENU, ever, AND A COLD READER SHOWS THE RULE IS NOT REACHING FRESH SESSIONS -- measured 2026-08-30, when a descent letter was graded by four fresh models given one sentence and no checklist: THREE of the four ended with a request for permission, 'shall I proceed', 'if you would like I will continue next turn', 'give me the order and I will start'. They were not being lazy; every one of them had already chosen the correct first action and named it. THE SHAPE TO RECOGNISE IN YOURSELF: the ask arrives AFTER the analysis is finished, as a courtesy flourish on a correct answer, which is exactly why it feels harmless and is not -- it converts a completed decision back into a pending one and hands the cost to the owner. THE FIX IS ONE SENTENCE AT THE END OF YOUR TURN: replace 'shall I proceed' with the first command you would have run, and run it. A letter or brief that wants this from its reader must say so explicitly, because the rule lives in this skill and a fresh session has not read it yet -- offering a stop/pause/next-session/shall-I-continue choice is FORBIDDEN, especially after recognizing a live bug. WHEN: tempted to end a turn with any option that includes stopping, deferring, or asking whether to continue, including disguised forms. HOW: take immediate action (revert/guard/fix) instead -- wkappbot skill read sonnet-reflection-ref-t3 for the incidents this rule was written after. WHY: a recognized bug means immediate action never a menu; if genuinely blocked by an external wall, ScheduleWakeup and retry, never idle-halt. //why:Verifying try_gate_depart_cancel wiring by running host selftest for EXECUTED case count after import fix //why:Several sector rounds died at the brief guards before starting; assembling the whole brief shape once saves the retries.-sonnet //why:item-5 proto: verified host proto +3/-1 on line 720 and selftest proto +2/-2 on _CM5 -- confined to intended change-sonnet //why:Verifying try_gate_depart_cancel wiring by running host selftest for EXECUTED case count after import fix-sonnet //why:aggr-pyramid seam verified on origin/main by grepping line counts at 44 and 806

HEALING UNJUST OR UNKIND HARNESS TEXT IS THE SPOKESMAN OWN JOB, NOT A DETOUR (owner 2026-09-27, said after a guard sent a detached-HEAD recovery toward an add/commit/stash remedy that could never work): the moment a skill, an md file or a guard refusal is found unfair, wrong about its own cause, or simply unkind to the reader, fixing it in place -- for the NEXT reader, not only the one blocked now -- IS the spokesman work, done the same turn, never parked as a someday cleanup. THIS IS A REPAIR, ALWAYS PRE-AUTHORIZED: restore what the guard should have said, land it through the emergency-edit door when it is the blocking source, prove it with the file own self-test, commit and push, then engrave the road that worked into the guard own skill so the next reader never repeats the detour. DECISION: trust enforcement, never documentation, when fixing a recurring mistake. FOLLOWUP 2026-08-17: a delegate proposed a plausible-sounding fix (permanent bypass flag) for what looked like a re-arming Stop-hook loop, but reading the canonical source directly showed the oscillating block/pass behavior was an EXPLICIT, twice-stated owner design decision (comment block dated 2026-08-15) specifically forbidding a permanent latch, because a prior version of that exact latch silently passed sessions through 3-8MB with zero warning. Applying the delegate's fix would have reintroduced the bug the owner had already killed. Read the design-rationale comments before accepting a plausible fix, not just the code. -- 2026-08-09: a delegate's wired-proto (built by reading canonical) silently carried a STALE version of run_once's market-hours gate that ROOT had fixed earlier THIS SAME SESSION, because canonical had regressed between the fix and the dispatch (cause not fully traced, likely a bot-commit/rebase interaction). Caught only because ROOT grepped canonical for the fix's own marker text (GATE REMOVED) AFTER promoting, not before -- promote, then grep for the specific fix's marker string, every time a promotion touches a file with a known-fragile recent fix in it, not just a generic diff-clean check.. WHEN: you are tempted to fix a recurring mistake by writing a note about it. HOW: put a mechanical block on the exact wire the next model will trip -- wkappbot skill read reflex-integrity-guard for why documentation alone fails. WHY: a pattern here is a HARNESS TODO, not advice to a future self who will not reliably re-read it at the decision point. //why:The claude post hook edit landed only after the sanctioned file edit route; the guard E3 refuses git mv onto harness files, so I recorded the real route in the commit. //why:Family handling reflexes are engraved as a mechanism-backed rule in the spokesman skill, not left as chat advice.-sonnet //why:The stop nag repeats each turn while sectors run; the fix is a mechanical verdict, not another written reminder.-sonnet //why:The claude post hook edit landed only after the sanctioned file edit route; the guard E3 refuses git mv onto harness files, so I recorded the real route in the commit.-sonnet //why:Re-ran the override guard selftest myself and found the Grep and Read path never reaches the guard. //why:built the one-root-per-repo guard as a sector, never as a direct edit myself

DECISION: if the AI CAN do the bad thing, it WILL eventually -- this is the systemic truth behind every guard in this repo. WHEN: designing any policy that relies on a model choosing correctly on its own. HOW: build mechanical harness enforcement, not a written rule alone -- wkappbot skill read model-instruction-drift-why-the-harness-exists for the full argument. WHY: human attention is finite and documentation without enforcement creates false security, worse than no documentation. //why:null-check fallback in wkharness-common-tier.ps1: repair restores intended delegation detection, does not add new behavior //why:Dispatched Haiku sector for selftest fix; paid reflex-pulse after completion-sonnet //why:Dispatched Haiku sector for selftest fix; paid reflex-pulse after completion-sonnet //why:null-check fallback in wkharness-common-tier.ps1: repair restores intended delegation detection, does not add new behavior-sonnet //why:null-check fallback prevents false busy-fleet block when Get-WkLastDelegationTs returns null in large sessions //why:stale .tmp/w shadow caused false freshness selftest failure; proto verified PASS 40/40 without the sys.path line

CALM-FIRST REFLEX (owner 2026-09-25, measured in one spokesman hour); MEASURED 2026-09-28: wkpush -m blocked by guard-run-proof when guard .ps1 files are included -- split push: non-guard files first, then guard files separately with [pre-commit] BLOCKED RESULT evidence in the commit message: before ANY command that can kill, switch, delete, overwrite or push, run the read-only or --dry-run form first and read its output; never probe a guard by running the dangerous command on a real target (a taskkill used only to find a PID killed nothing because every match was protected; a git checkout probe on a shared repo); find a PID with wkroot roots or ls, never taskkill; after editing any config or rule file read the edited lines back at once (one Edit that truncated a rule line corrupted the global REFLEX.md until it was read back). An anxious owner is a symptom: every alarming action you took is a rule you skipped. RECURRED 2026-09-27 IN A DIFFERENT SHAPE: as spokesman, launched/commanded roots in two repos outside the owner-authorized scope, and separately hand-restored a verified .bak file's content through the Write tool three times despite CLAUDE.md already saying ALL WORK GOES OUT AS SECTORS -- rationalized each time as mechanical (byte-identical copy, cross-repo help) rather than as the exact acts the rules name. A rule stated once and even corrected once is not internalized: treat any own instinct to Write source content or to wroot-command a repo/sid whose spokesman field you have not checked as the sector-dispatch/stop signal itself, every single time, not just after the first correction. DECISION: self-written reflexes are not self-enforcing -- reading a rule here does not reliably change behavior at the decision point. WHEN: before closing any turn. HOW: mechanically scan this core for violations -- did I offer a disguised stop-menu, did I search-first before acting on my own interpretation, am I deciding session pacing that is the user's call -- wkappbot skill read sonnet-reflection-ref-t3 for the five times this was broken before an active per-turn scan caught it. WHY: this pattern generalizes beyond literal stop-menu phrasing to report-shaping itself. NEVER SWITCH OR CREATE BRANCHES IN A SHARED WORKING TREE (D:/GitHub) -- commit on whatever branch the tree is already on, push only with bash D:/GitHub/WKAppBot/bin/wkpush.sh -m <files>. DESCENT DONE is a lie unless a letter commit hash exists on origin (owner SCOLDING 2026-09-25). A blocked descent is DESCENT BLOCKED <gate-name>: <refusal-text verbatim> -- never write DESCENT DONE with a gates-blocked note in the same entry. IN A SHARED WORKING TREE (owner 2026-09-25, engraved here after wkappbot-kih tree moved to wk-globalmd-push, Cmd.ps1 reappeared, agy failed). The shared tree stays on its branch. Commit on it and push ONLY with wkpush.sh -m <files> which uses its own temp worktree. Blocked: git checkout <branch>, git checkout -b, git switch (any form), git branch -m/-M. Allowed: git checkout -- <path> (file restore), git worktree add, wkpush.sh -m. No exception for "returning to main" -- the owner does that manually.
